title: Three Buttons
statement: A calculator shows the number $1$ and has exactly three buttons: one multiplies the number shown by $2$, one multiplies it by $3$, and one multiplies it by $5$. A student presses the buttons one at a time until the calculator shows $180$. Every number shown after a press must be even. How many different sequences of button presses are possible?
hints: Write $180$ as a product of primes. What does this tell you about how many times each button must be pressed?

Since $180 = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$, the buttons used are fixed and only their order can vary. Counting orders in which some items are identical is a problem of permutations with repetition, but first you must work out which orders the evenness rule allows.

The first press shows $2$, $3$ or $5$, so it must be the $2$-button. An even number stays even when multiplied by any whole number, so the rule places no restriction on later presses. Now count the orders of the four presses $2, 3, 3, 5$, where swapping the two $3$-presses gives the same sequence.
solution:
Since $180=2^2\cdot3^2\cdot5$, every valid sequence uses the $2$-button twice, the $3$-button twice and the $5$-button once. The number increases with each press, so $180$ is reached only on the last press.

The first number shown is the first button's value, so the first press must be $2$. After that the number is even and stays even under multiplication, so the parity condition affects only the first press.

The remaining presses are one $2$, two $3$s and one $5$ in any order, giving $\frac{4!}{2!}=12$ sequences.
